title: Delamination in Large REBCO Coils
authors: Jun Lu, Yan Xin, Iain Dixon, Brent Jarvis, Kwangmin Kim, Yu Suetomi, Jeremy Levitan, Jan Jaroszynski, Hongyu Bai
abstract: REBCO coated conductors have been used in ultrahigh field magnets for condensed matter physics research, nuclear fusion, particle accelerators, and NMR applications. It is well known, however, that they are not mechanically strong against delamination due to their intrinsic layered structures. As a result, the delamination issue has become one of the major design challenges of REBCO magnet coils. As a part of the development of the 40 T all-superconducting magnet at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, USA, large-scale coils wound by two-in-hand REBCO conductor with turn-to-turn insulation was designed and tested at 4.2 K in an 11.4 T background magnetic field. We found REBCO degradations within the windings and at the crossover joints during the tests. The postmortem inspection found that the degradation was caused by delamination. The delamination appears on the surface of the conductor as bubbles which were subsequently studied by microscopy. Additionally, a similar bubble was found on a short sample by torque magnetometry. This supports the inference that the delamination bubbles found in coils are due to electromagnetic stress. In this paper, we present these findings. The implication of these findings for future magnet designs and the method of mitigation will be discussed.
summary: This paper investigates delamination failures in large REBCO superconducting coils used for ultrahigh field magnets. Through extensive testing and postmortem analysis, the authors conclusively demonstrate that these structural failures are caused by electromagnetic stress from transport currents. The findings are crucial for improving the design and reliability of next-generation high-field superconducting magnets.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical issue of delamination in large REBCO coated conductors, which severely limits the design and performance of ultrahigh field superconducting magnets.
main_result: Delamination bubbles observed in large coils are strongly attributed to electromagnetic stress induced by transport and screening currents, a mechanism confirmed via torque magnetometry.
method: The study combines large-scale magnet testing, postmortem inspection using microscopy, and controlled mechanical testing via torque magnetometry.
model_or_system: The physical system involves REBCO coated conductors wound into large-scale coils designed for 40 T magnets. The analysis focuses on the mechanical integrity of the layered structure under high magnetic fields and associated currents.
key_observables: Surface bubbles, degradation of critical current (Ic), crack propagation paths, and sudden drops in measured torque values.
important_parameters: Operating fields up to 11.4 T (and implied higher fields), measured delamination strengths ($\sim 2.5$ to $3.8$ MPa), and the magnitude of electromagnetic stress.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the observed degradation is directly caused by electromagnetic stress, and that the torque magnetometry setup can accurately reproduce this failure mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical evidence of delamination, including SEM/TEM cross-sections showing cracks, and torque magnetometry results demonstrating bubble formation and collapse upon chemical removal.
paper_structure: The paper presents findings from testing large coils, detailing the observation of degradation, followed by mechanistic investigation using microscopy and torque magnetometry to prove the link between electromagnetic stress and delamination, concluding with design implications.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science, the analysis of failure under extreme, non-equilibrium electromagnetic stress and the development of mitigation strategies for superconducting devices are relevant to understanding material limits in quantum technology infrastructure.
